summary: Gustaf John Ramstedt was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He completed his M.A. at the University of Helsinki (ca. 1893–1898) under Otto Donner, J. N. Reuter, and Eemil Nestor Setälä, later serving there as professor (1917–1941).

Gustav Bickell was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Halle and earned his Ph.D. at Marburg (1857–1862). He held posts at Marburg, Münster, Innsbruck, and the University of Vienna, where he was professor of Semitic languages from 1891.

Gustav Ecke specialized in Sinology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Bonn, Berlin, and Erlangen-Nuremberg (Ph.D. 1922), he taught at Xiamen, Tsinghua, and Fu Jen universities before serving as professor of arts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1950–1966).

Gustav Friedrich Oehler was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed a Ph.D. at Tübingen and studied at Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held posts at Tübingen, the Basel Mission Seminary, Schöntal Seminary, and the University of Breslau.

Gustav Haloun was a Sinologist and Central Asian scholar. He earned his doctorate at Leipzig under August Conrady and habilitated in Prague. Haloun directed at Göttingen (1931–1938) and served as Chair of Chinese Language and History at Cambridge (1938–1951).

Gustav Herbig was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and Munich, earning his Ph.D. and habilitation there. After working as a librarian at the Bavarian State Library (1899–1913), he held professorships at the universities of Rostock, Breslau, and Munich.

Gustav Mensching worked in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Göttingen, Berlin, and Marburg under Rudolf Otto and Friedrich Heiler, he held faculty posts at Marburg, the University of Latvia, Kiel University, and the University of Bonn.

Gustav Meyer was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. Following teaching posts and a position at Charles University, he served as professor for Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at the University of Graz (1877–1897).

Gustav Roth was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctorate at Munich (1949–1952) under Helmut Hoffmann and Paul Thieme. He later worked as Akademischer Oberrat at Göttingen (1965–1981) and served as Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Gustav Salomon Oppert was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Halle-Wittenberg. He worked at the Bodleian Library and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency University (1872–1894) and Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1895).

Gustave Liétard, an Indologist and historian-archaeologist, earned a Dr.med. at the University of Strasbourg (ca. 1853–1858) and studied under Frédéric-Guillaume Bergmann and Philippe Édouard Foucaux.
Gustavo Benavides is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies whose academic affiliation at Villanova University is attested in 1995 and 2004.

Gustavo Moura is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned degrees from the University of Chester and Federal University of Paraíba, completing his PhD in Religious Studies at Wilfrid Laurier University in 2022.

Gustaw Blatt was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Jagiellonian University under Lucjan Malinowski and at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann, Ernst Windisch, and August Leskien. He served as Privatdozent and Professor of comparative Indo-European grammar at the University of Lviv.

Guus Kroonen is a linguist who studied for his doctorate under Alexander Lubotsky. He has held positions at the University of Copenhagen (ca. 2013) and at Leiden University's Centre for Linguistics (2016).

Guy Bugault, a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, studied under Olivier Lacombe. He held posts at Paris Nanterre University and Paris-Sorbonne University, where he served as Professor of Indian and Comparative Philosophy (ca. 1968–1985).

Guy G. Stroumsa is a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Harvard. He held long-term academic posts at Hebrew University and served as Professor of the Study of Abrahamic Religions at Oxford (2009–2013).

Guy Newland is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who received his PhD from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. His faculty career includes serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University (attested 1996–2010).
Guybon Henry Damant was an Indologist and linguist who completed his M.A. at Christ's College, Cambridge (1864–1868), studying under John Peile and Edward Byles Cowell.
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
